name: Droggn
description: Droggn is a rare Tyrolean trick-taking game from the Stubai Valley, historically played with a unique 66-card Tarock deck. It is a descendant of the Tarock L'Hombre family, making it distinct from more common Austrian variants like KÃ¶nigrufen. Known for its specific Tyrolean dialect terminology and the tactical use of the 'Fox' card, the game survived in the alpine villages of Fulpmes and Telfes as a testament to localized card-playing traditions.

history.origins: The game is centered in the Stubaital (Stubai Valley) southwest of Innsbruck. Its introduction is shrouded in legend, with roots potentially tied to Tyrolean resistance hero Andreas Hofer or traveling Italian merchants.
timeline: 1800s: Traditional Tarock patterns begin to specialize in alpine valleys.
Early 20th Century: Specific 66-card packs for Droggn were commercially available.
1990s: Rules formalized and archived to prevent extinction of the Stubai tradition.
history.cultural: Integral to Tyrolean tavern culture; the term 'Droggn' effectively means 'the local way of playing Tarock'.
history.evolution: Preserves game mechanics from the early 19th century L'Hombre games that disappeared elsewhere in the Habsburg Empire.

setup.deck: 66-card deck (Industrie und Glück pattern with lowest cards removed). 22 Tarocks, 44 suit cards.
setup.dealing: 21 cards per player, dealt in batches of 7. 3-card talon face down in centre.

rules.objective: As declarer, take at least 37 card points (half of 74) in tricks to win the contract.
rules.gameplay:
1. Bidding: Players compete for the contract.
2. Talon Exchange: Declarer can swap cards with the blind.
3. Trick Play: High and low Pip rankings exist. Tarocks always win. Follow suit required; Trumping required if void.
keyRules: The Gstieß (fool) is not a trump; it may be played anytime and never wins except last trick of Super Mord.
Ultimo: A bonus for winning the final trick with the weakest trump (card I, der Kleine).
Point total in pack: 74 card points (counted in threes, minus 2 per group).

strategy.basic: Keep track of the 22 trumps. If you are the declarer, try to clear the defenders' trumps as early as possible.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Fox' play: Intentionally keeping a low card (singleton) to bait defenders into revealing their high court cards.
strategy.advanced: Declarer should keep a long suit to pull trumps, while defenders should try to 'sandwich' the declarer so they play first into a new suit.
tips: Defenders should smear points when their partner wins a trick.

variations.name: Deal and talon position
variations.description: Talon may be dealt in the middle (e.g. after second batch of 7) rather than at end. One variant: deal in batches of 5-5-5-3-3 then talon.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Deal and talon placement do not change engine constants; variant is descriptive only.

variations.name: Exposing the talon
variations.description: In ordinary game some players have declarer expose the talon before picking it up; in Solo declarer picks up without showing. Others say declarer never shows the talon.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Talon visibility is a procedural variant not modelled as engine overrides.

variations.name: Game with 78 cards
variations.description: Played with full 78-card pack. Deal in 5s; declarer needs 39 card points to win. Super Mord score probably 169. Otherwise rules same.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: 78-card variant would require different deck and deal constants; not yet modelled.
